title: Find a positive global matrix constant after T080
objective: Prove or refute the dimension-uniform sharp candidate K(A)>=(mu/2)A^{-1} for every unit-diagonal SPD A. The signed-rank-one interior family rules out every larger global constant. In parallel, study the distinct sharp boundary candidate K0(C)>=(3/2)P_ker(C). A proof of any positive global constant yields O((n/mu) log(1/epsilon)) without claiming the sharper covariance-rate conjecture.
acceptance_checks: Uses the full Loewner or equivalent Schur-complement inequality, not only kernel compression unless symmetry proves the kernel direction is reducing.
Reproduces the exact n=8 constants 1057837/531441 and the independent subset-DP audit.
Treats the two-pole plus k-simplex family with explicit quantifier order k to infinity followed by latitude to zero.
Distinguishes the boundary upper constant 3/2 from the global positive-mu constant, which cannot exceed 1 because A=I.
Reproduces the signed-rank-one formula showing that no global constant above 1/2 is possible, including the n=9 exact counterexample to gamma(A)>=mu.
Directly attacks gamma(A)>=mu/2 over two-scale degenerations rather than assuming a pointwise boundary limit is uniform.
Does not rely on bare Jensen alone: the equicorrelation n=21, mu=9/20 barrier and its vanishing fixed-mu asymptotic are reproduced.
Does not replace the full average by word/reverse-word pairs: the rank-one n=9 kernel quotient 3/8 barrier is reproduced.
Distinguishes a positive universal complexity constant from the refuted sharp coefficient 2 and from C001.
A positive result includes a uniform finite-positive-mu transfer or explicitly isolates that remaining uniformity gap.
